Course Description

Calendar Description for ECE 190

Introduction to electrical and computer engineering with an emphasis on the profession of engineering, and engineering design. Topics include engineering design, safety, risk analysis, engineering data analysis, project management, sustainability, business, entrepreneurship, and intellectual property. Additional topics include co-op fundamentals for engineering students, professional development, and diversity training with a goal of understanding the roles and responsibilities of the professional engineer in society.

View requirements for ECE 190

Course workload:  ECE190 is a 0.25 unit weight course, which is half the normal course weight.  It is expected that students should put in, on average, about 3 to 4 hours of work per week for this course.

Instructor acknowledgements:  Thank you to Professors David Wang and Bill Bishop for sharing their ECE190 course materials to help me prepare for this course.  Also, all images in the course slides are taken from https://pixabay.com except where otherwise noted.

Learning Outcomes

By the end of this course students should be able to:
(1) Explain and apply techniques needed to succeed in Waterloo Engineering
(2) Describe the engineering profession, including its scope and its most essential features
(3) Work professionally in a small team
(4) Describe the steps of the engineering design process and apply them to a small design project
(5) Define sustainable development and describe ways in which environmental sustainability and engineering are related
(6) Explain the three design-team traps of ignorance, staleness, and social loafing and identify techniques to help avoid them
(7) Explain the central ethical duties in engineering, and make justifiable decisions to resolve ethical dilemmas
(8) Analyze and control risks in simple engineering and workplace settings
(9) Define professional development and explain the role of professional development in engineering
(10) Characterize entrepreneurship as a career path for engineers, and list entrepreneurship opportunities at Waterloo
(11) Describe the three components of project management, construct a PERT chart, and identify a project's critical path
(12) Explain the measurement-error notions of systematic error, random error, precision, and accuracy, and perform calculations with uncertain numbers

Class attendance policy:  In ECE190 you are required to attend all scheduled in-person group activities and to attend any other meetings organized by your group.  Attendance at lectures is strongly encouraged:  you can expect to learn the material better, and to do significantly better on the exam and group activities, if you attend the lectures in person.  To increase lecture engagement, you should write down key points in your own words – I provide lecture summary sheets on LEARN that can be used for this purpose.

Group membership:  About 40% of the grades in this course are based on work that students do in small groups.  Group membership is assigned randomly in LEARN, and on LEARN you can find a list of students in your group.  The course instructor reserves the right to change group membership at any time in the term to balance group sizes, to deal with course enrollment changes, to deal with group members who have a history of being absent or non-participation, or for any other reason.  However, changes to group membership are expected to occur only rarely, and requests from students to change groups will not be granted except in extreme circumstances. The course instructor also has the right to change who acts as the coordinator in a group.

Grading policy for Short Video assignment:  This deliverable is individually assessed.  Missing the deadline by up to 1 hour results in a grade reduction of 25% of the possible marks, while missing it by up to 24 hours results in a grade reduction of 50% of the possible marks, and beyond that the grade reduction is 100%.  These grade reductions may be reduced or waived at the course instructor's discretion, but only in cases where the student submits a short-term absence (self-declared on https://absence.uwaterloo.ca with one of the two days overlapping the assignment deadline), or submits a religious or creed-related absence (self-declared on https://absence.uwaterloo.ca with the dates overlapping the assignment deadline), or has an approved absence due to severe illness (submit documents on https://absence.uwaterloo.ca), or in other extreme extenuating circumstances (e.g., attending a relative's funeral) approved by the course instructor.   

Grading policy for Group Agreement Form:  Students whose names are missing from the submitted form will be individually assessed late submission penalties.  Missing the deadline by up to 1 hour results in a grade reduction of 25% of the possible marks, while missing it by up to 24 hours results in a grade reduction of 50% of the possible marks, and beyond that the grade reduction is 100%.  These grade reductions may be reduced or waived at the course instructor's discretion, but only in cases where the student submits a short-term absence (self-declared on https://absence.uwaterloo.ca with one of the two days overlapping the assignment deadline), or submits a religious or creed-related absence (self-declared on https://absence.uwaterloo.ca with the dates overlapping the assignment deadline), or has an approved absence due to severe illness (submit documents on https://absence.uwaterloo.ca), or in other extreme extenuating circumstances (e.g., attending a relative's funeral) approved by the course instructor.   

Grading policy for Deliverables 1 (Part 1), 1 (Part 2), 2, 3, and 4:

  • Late submission policy:  Grade reductions for submitting a group report late are normally applied to all group members, not just to the group coordinator.  Missing the deadline by up to 1 hour results in a grade reduction of 25% of the possible marks, while missing it by up to 24 hours results in a grade reduction of 50% of the possible marks, and beyond that the grade reduction is 100%.  These grade reductions will not be reduced or waived for students who self-declare short-term absences on https://absence.uwaterloo.ca. However, the grade reductions may be reduced or waived at the course instructor's discretion in cases where every group member submits a religious or creed-related absence (self-declared on https://absence.uwaterloo.ca with the dates overlapping the assignment deadline), or has an approved absence due to severe illness (submit documents on https://absence.uwaterloo.ca), or in other extreme extenuating circumstances (e.g., attending a relative's funeral) approved by the course instructor.  In no case will a report be accepted more than three days after the due date.

  • Policy about attendance information included in each report:  A grade deduction of 10% of the possible marks will be applied to the group grade of a report if the attendance photo including in the report is missing or unlabelled or if the attendance information provided in the report is incomplete, inconsistent, or inaccurate. The grade reduction may be reduced or waived at the course instructor's discretion.

  • Students in a group normally receive identical grades for group reports, with the following exceptions:

    • Late arrival at a group activity:  A student who attends a group activity but is late (that is, they miss the attendance photo taken during the first two minutes of the activity) will be given a grade reduction. The grade reduction applies just to the individual student, not the group. The grade reduction is 5% of the possible marks for the first occurrence, 10% of the possible marks for the second occurrence, 20% of the possible marks for the third occurrence, and 40% of the possible marks for the fourth occurrence. These grade reductions may be reduced or waived at the course instructor's discretion if there are reasonable extenuating circumstances (such as a bus breakdown or a co-op interview) that are indicated on the submitted report.

    • Non-participation in a group activity:  A student who attends a group activity but doesn’t participate in a meaningful way may be given a grade reduction for non-participation.  The grade reduction applies to just the individual, not the group.  The grade reduction is normally 50% of the possible marks for the first occurrence, 75% of the possible marks for the second occurrence, and 100% of the possible marks for subsequent occurrences.  The course instructor may remove a non-participating student from their group (see the Group membership section above).

    • Missing a group activity:  A student who misses an entire group activity will receive a grade of zero on that activity. This grade reduction applies to just the individual, not the group.  This grade reduction may be reduced or waived at the course instructor's discretion, but only in cases where the student submits a short-term absence (self-declared on https://absence.uwaterloo.ca with one of the two days overlapping the activity date), or submits a religious or creed-related absence (self-declared on https://absence.uwaterloo.ca with the dates overlapping the activity date), or has an approved absence due to severe illness (submit documents on https://absence.uwaterloo.ca), or in other extreme extenuating circumstances (e.g., attending a relative's funeral) approved by the course instructor.  In cases where a group activity is missed and the grade reduction is reduced or waived, the course instructor may shift some or all of the weight of the activity (for the individual student, not the group) to the final exam. The course instructor may remove a repeatedly-absent student from their group (see the Group membership section above).

Rules for permitted aids and collaboration on group activities:  Group activities and associated reports are to be done collaboratively by members within each group.  You may access any of the course materials provided on LEARN.  You also may look up topics in textbooks or access non-AI-generated content on the internet, but:

  • You may not use AI/ML/LLM tools (ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini, Claude, google "AI Overview", Duck.ai, etc.)

  • You may not use “homework services” (chegg.com, coursehero.com, etc.)

  • You may not post activity questions or answers on social media or websites.

  • You may not share your activity answers (directly or indirectly) with anyone except those who are in your group and the course teaching team.

For each group deliverable, groups will have to declare whether or not they followed these rules. Failure to make the declaration results in grade reduction of 50% of the possible marks. Violation of the rules results in a grade reduction of up to 100% of the possible marks and, in serious cases, possible academic discipline under Policy 71.

Incorrect dropbox policy:  In general, students are responsible for submitting their work in the correct LEARN dropbox.  For group reports, the group coordinator must use the dropbox intended for their group and section.  Reports are not considered to be “submitted” until they are submitted in the correct LEARN dropbox.  Work submitted to the incorrect dropbox will not be graded and, in due course, will be deleted.

Multiple submission policy:  If more than one submission is made, only the most recent submission will be graded.

Deadline to raise concerns or questions about grades:  As soon as grades for a given activity are released, a LEARN announcement will be posted stating a deadline and the relevant person to contact with any concerns or questions about grading.  In most cases, the deadline will be about a week after the grades are released.  Concerns or questions that are raised after the posted deadline will not be considered.

Midterm test and final exam information:  Both the midterm test and final exam are written in-person, with dates and times and locations to be announced as soon as they are known.  Assigned seating is used, with details available at https://odyssey.uwaterloo.ca/teaching/schedule.  The midterm test and final exam are closed-book, written individually, and consist of randomized multiple-choice questions based on the slide decks covered in the course lectures.  Additional details are as follows: 

  • Midterm test: 

    • Duration:  1 hour

    • Question format:  41 randomized multiple-choice questions

    • Tip:  Bring a pencil and eraser to the test so that you can change your answers if needed.

    • Content:  The midterm test covers material on the weekly ECE190 lecture slide decks from:
             Week 1 (Tues lecture, only slides in the "boilerplate" and "Overview of ECE" sections)
             Week 2 (both the Tues and Thurs lectures)
             Week 4 (Tues lecture)
             Week 5 (Tues lecture)
      When studying, focus on what is on the slides – you do not have to look up or study webpages or papers or videos or textbook sections that are cited on the slides. 

    • Permitted aids:  The only permitted aids are...

      • A non-programmable calculator.

      • One double-sided aid sheet handwritten on normal 8.5 x 11 inch paper.

        • You must individually prepare your own aid sheet.

        • You must prepare your aid sheet entirely by writing with physical pen or pencil on physical paper. (Specifically, you may not use software and a printer to create any part of your aid sheet. Exceptions will be considered only if a request is made on medical grounds through AccessAbility Services.)

        • Aid sheets may be inspected during the midterm. A grade reduction of up to 25% of the possible midterm marks will be applied if your aid sheet violates the above requirements.

    • Missed midterm:  No make-up or alternatively-scheduled midterm is being offered in this course.  The only reasons deemed valid for missing the midterm are a short-term absence (self-declared on https://absence.uwaterloo.ca with one of the two days overlapping the test date), a religious or creed-related absence (self-declared on https://absence.uwaterloo.ca with the dates overlapping the test date), an approved absence due to severe illness (submit documents on https://absence.uwaterloo.ca), or other extreme extenuating circumstances (e.g., attending a relative's funeral) approved by the course instructor.  If the midterm is missed due to a valid reason, the weight of the final exam is increased from 35% to 55%. A midterm that is missed without a valid reason counts as if the midterm was written with an earned grade of zero.

  • Final exam: 

    • Duration:  2 hours

    • Question format:  72 randomized multiple-choice questions

    • Tip:  Bring a pencil and eraser to the exam so that you can change your answers if needed.

    • Content:  The final exam is comprehensive, covering material from the ECE190 lecture slide decks in Weeks 2 (both lectures), 4, 5, 8-13.  When studying, focus on what is on the slides – you do not have to look up or study webpages or papers or videos or textbook sections that are cited on the slides.  Note that the weeks are not weighted equally on the exam:
             Lightly weighted (4-5 multiple choice questions):  Weeks 2 (Tues lecture), 2 (Thurs lecture), 8, 11
             Medium weighted (6-8 multiple choice questions):  Weeks 4, 5, 12
             Heavily weighted (9-11 multiple choice questions):  Weeks 9, 10, 13

    • Permitted aids:  The only permitted aids are...

      • A non-programmable calculator.

      • Two double-sided aid sheets handwritten on normal 8.5 x 11 inch paper.

        • You must individually prepare your own aid sheets.

        • You must prepare your aid sheets entirely by writing with physical pen or pencil on physical paper. (Specifically, you may not use software and a printer to create any part of your aid sheets. Exceptions will be considered only if a request is made on medical grounds through AccessAbility Services.)

        • Aid sheets will be collected at the end of the exam and inspected. A grade reduction of up to 25% of the possible exam marks will be applied if either of your aid sheets violates the above requirements or if you do not submit your aid sheets at the end of the exam.

    • Missed exam:  The only reasons deemed valid for missing the final exam are a religious or creed-related absence (self-declared on https://absence.uwaterloo.ca with the dates overlapping the exam date), an approved absence due to severe illness (submit documents on https://absence.uwaterloo.ca), or other extreme extenuating circumstances (e.g., attending a relative's funeral) approved by the course instructor. If the final exam is missed for a valid reason, the student will be granted a deferred exam. If the final exam is missed without a valid reason, the exam grade will be considered to be zero and the final course grade calculated accordingly. A student who misses any final exam should contact the First-Year Engineering Office as soon as possible.

Administrative Policy

If TA resources or TA availability are unexpectedly reduced, some deliverables may be graded on a simplified basis.

Accreditation Data Collection

The Faculty of Engineering may be collecting information from this course for accreditation purposes, including course outline, exams, assignments, and samples of student work. The Canadian Engineering Accreditation Board (CEAB) periodically reviews the Bachelor of Applied Science (BASc) and the Bachelor of Software Engineering (BSE) degrees. The Canadian Architectural Certification Board (CACB) periodically reviews the Bachelor of Architectural Studies (BAS) degree and the Master of Architecture (MArch) degree.

University Policy

Mental Health: At the University of Waterloo, we are dedicated to supporting your mental and emotional well-being. Our Counselling Services offer confidential support, including individual counselling, workshops, and crisis intervention.
If you're struggling, please reach out for help at 519-888-4096 or visit their website for more information.

Academic integrity: In order to maintain a culture of academic integrity, members of the University of Waterloo community are expected to promote honesty, trust, fairness, respect and responsibility.

Grievance: A student who believes that a decision affecting some aspect of their university life has been unfair or unreasonable may have grounds for initiating a grievance. Read Policy 70, Student Petitions and Grievances, Section 4. When in doubt, please be certain to contact the department’s administrative assistant who will provide further assistance.

Discipline: A student is expected to know what constitutes academic integrity to avoid committing an academic offence, and to take responsibility for their actions. A student who is unsure whether an action constitutes an offence, or who needs help in learning how to avoid offences (e.g., plagiarism, cheating) or about “rules” for group work/collaboration should seek guidance from the course instructor, academic advisor, or the undergraduate associate dean. For information on categories of offences and types of penalties, students should refer to Policy 71, Student Discipline. For typical penalties, check Guidelines for the Assessment of Penalties.

Appeals: A decision made or penalty imposed under Policy 70, Student Petitions and Grievances (other than a petition) or Policy 71, Student Discipline may be appealed if there is a ground. A student who believes they have a ground for an appeal should refer to Policy 72, Student Appeals.

Note for students with disabilities and disabling conditions: The University of Waterloo recognizes its obligations under the Ontario Human Rights Code to accommodate students with known or suspected disabilities and disabling conditions (e.g. medical conditions, injuries, impacts of trauma such as from violence or discrimination) to the point of undue hardship. To support this obligation, AccessAbility Services (AAS) collaborates with all academic departments and schools to facilitate academic accommodations for students with disabilities and disabling conditions without compromising the academic integrity of the curriculum. If you believe you may require academic accommodations (e.g., testing accommodations, classroom accommodations), register with AAS as early in the term as possible by completing the online application. Students already registered with AAS must activate their accommodations for each of their courses at the beginning of each term using AAS' online system. If you require assistance, contact AAS by phone (519-888-4567 ext. 35082), email (instructor@example.com) or in-person (Needles Hall North, 1st Floor, Room 1401). 

Turnitin.com: Text matching software (Turnitin®) may be used to screen assignments in this course. Turnitin® is used to verify that all materials and sources in assignments are documented. Students' submissions are stored on a U.S. server, therefore students must be given an alternative (e.g., scaffolded assignment or annotated bibliography), if they are concerned about their privacy and/or security. Students will be given due notice, in the first week of the term and/or at the time assignment details are provided, about arrangements and alternatives for the use of Turnitin in this course.

It is the responsibility of the student to notify the instructor if they, in the first week of term or at the time assignment details are provided, wish to submit alternate assignment.
